Key audit matter:
The fair value of the Group’s investment property
(buildings) is classified as Level 3 in the fair value
hierarchy, due to the use of unobservable inputs that
involve inherent estimation uncertainty.
The valuation under the discounted cash flow
approach, involves significant estimates and
assumptions of unobservable inputs in the valuation
model such as projected future cash flows, future rent
escalations, exit capitalisation rates and the discount
rates.
We identified the valuation of investment property
using the discounted cash flow method, as a key audit
matter due to the significant judgement and estimation
involved in management’s use of unobservable inputs
and assumptions.
How our audit addressed the Key audit ma:
We engaged our own valuation specialists to assist with:
• Evaluating the reasonableness of the inputs used in the
discounted cash flow model. This included:
» Assessing the accuracy of the projected future cash
flows used in the valuation model to supporting lease
contracts and historical expenditure patterns based on
prior year actual costs and the projected inflationary
adjustments to costs.
» Challenging the appropriateness of the discount rates
and exit capitalisation rates used in the valuation by
comparing the discount rate to market rates and exit
capitalisation rates to available industry data, taking
into consideration comparability to housing indices and
market factors.
We assessed the appropriateness and adequacy of the
disclosures related to the valuation of investment properties in
the consolidated financial statements, in accordance with IFRS
13, Fair Value Measurement.
